mentions.name: Micro
mentions.description: Micro is a long-running personal project that started as a Go framework and has evolved into a personal assistant and home server, pursuing the original mission of being a Google alternative or superapp. It currently has a PWA and an Android app is being worked on.
mentions.problem: The author keeps trying to kill the project but it won't go away, and it probably needs a ground-up rewrite.
mentions.audience: Not really for anyone else at the moment; the author posts it publicly but it is currently for their own use.
mentions.source_excerpt: Almost 12 years on Micro https://micro.mu. something I keep trying to kill and won't go away. Started as a Go framework now more of a personal assistant and home server.

evidence.value: Almost 12 years on Micro https://micro.mu. something I keep trying to kill and won't go away. Started as a Go framework now more of a personal assistant and home server.
evidence.author: asim

mentions.name: Micro
mentions.description: Micro is a personal AI agent that the author has iterated from tools into an assistant, now aiming to make it generally useful. It runs as a single Go binary with no separate frontend and can be self-hosted from the provided repository.
mentions.problem: Existing AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini don't offer what the author wants; the project aims to be a generally useful personal alternative.
mentions.audience: Personal users looking for a self-hostable AI agent as an alternative to mainstream assistants.
mentions.source_excerpt: Micro - a personal AI agent - https://micro.mu

evidence.value: Micro - a personal AI agent - https://micro.mu

mentions.name: Mu
mentions.description: An MCP server and web app that provides real-time access to news, markets, weather, video, places, search, and other key tools and services behind a single API and access token for AI agents.
mentions.source_excerpt: Mu - Tools for Agents. An MCP server and web app that provides real time access to news, markets, weather, video, places, search, etc. It's sort of extension of a previous idea I had to put all the key tools and services behind a single api and access token.
